text:
lina: heads-up — noticed a perf regression + intermittent NaNs after the fp8 kernel selector landed on canary. repro on long-context chat workload (seq_len ~ 4096). profile attached in thread.

kevin: ugh. do we have a minimal repro? is it deterministic or flakey? which kernels picked?

lina: repro is pretty consistent on canary with traffic replay. selector tends to pick fp8_gemm_v2 for qkv when sequence < 512, but for long contexts it sometimes picks mixed-fp8 path due to our latency heuristics. observed NaNs showing up from kv_cache tensors after a few token steps. example log: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:42:08Z] kernel_choice: fp8_gemm_v2 selected for qkv matmul
[2026-03-15T12:42:08Z] nan-detect: kv_cache[layer=7] contains NaN at step=24
[2026-03-15T12:42:08Z] fallback: none (selector assumed safe)
```

lina: perf summary (canary): before selector: 1.23k tok/s, p95 86ms. after selector umi: 1.05k tok/s, p95 112ms. plus ~0.4% requests hit NaN and error out.

dario: two axes: numeric stability (NaN) and selector heuristic (perf regress). for NaNs, smoothquant-style rescaling or increasing clip limits on calibration usually helps. did we reuse the same calibration profile for long-context tests?

maya: quick check: try nan-to-num on kv cache as a band-aid and force-fp16 kernel for the batch that triggered NaNs. e.g.:
```
# pseudocode
if torch.isnan(kv_cache).any():
    kv_cache = torch.nan_to_num(kv_cache, nan=0.0, posinf=1e6, neginf=-1e6)
    route_to_kernel('fp16_fallback')
```

kevin: that's fine short-term but we need a fix at the kernel/quant layer. possible causes: 1) fp8 requantization scale underflow/overflow, 2) per-tensor vs per-channel scales mismatch after fused ops, 3) accumulators/rescale ordering in our fused QKV kernel.

perf-bench: repro profile attached:
```
-- baseline (fp16 only): qkv_matmul 12.3ms, softmax 2.1ms, kv_write 1.4ms
-- selector-on (fp8 path): qkv_matmul(fp8_gemm_v2) 13.8ms, dequantize 1.9ms, kv_write 2.9ms
-- observed: extra dequant/req cost + occasional nan detection cost + retries
```

perf-bench: also saw that fp8 path does extra per-block scaling for smoothquant calibration (we used a small calibration set). increasing calibration samples for long-context reduces NaN frequency but doesn't fully remove perf hit.

dario: actionable items from my side:
- audit fp8 kernel for correct accumulation dtype (float32 accum) and stable requant path
- add per-channel fallback when scale variance > threshold
- add a guard in kernel selector: avoid fp8 for seq_len > 1024 OR when kv_reuse_ratio > 0.25

lina: +1 to selector guard. current heuristic was too eager since it favored smaller memory footprint over sustained throughput.

kevin: also add a cheap pre-pass that scans qkv outputs for extreme values before writing to kv_cache, with an inexpensive clamp: clamp(x, -clamp_val, clamp_val). we used clamp_val=6.0 in calibration; try bumping to 8.0.

maya: FYI I pushed a small canary: if nan rate > 0.1% in last minute, flip selector to conservative mode (fp16/int8 only) and emit alert. ops-bot reported the deploy: "deploy: selector-tweak v0.3 -> canary" :rocket:

ops-bot: deploy event: selector-tweak v0.3 promoted to canary at 2026-03-15T13:05:00Z.

lina: test notes — when I re-ran with smoothquant per-channel calibration and longer calibration set (500 samples) NaN events dropped ~10x but p95 still high vs baseline. this indicates remaining overhead comes from extra rescale/dequant ops in path.

dario: long-term: try to fuse dequant+kv_write to avoid materializing large tensors and reduce memory traffic. also look into quantized attention kernels that keep keys/values in quantized form and only dequantize on-demand for outputs.

kevin: for short-term patch:
1) add selector guard for seq_len and kv_reuse_ratio
2) add clamp pre-pass + nan-to-num fallback in runtime
3) require larger calibration set for fp8 on canary

lina: I'll own rollout. planning: apply guard + clamp pre-pass to canary now, monitor for 30m, then widen if stable. will attach updated profiling after run. :eyes: :thumbsup:

perf-bench: after canary patch (30m): 1.18k tok/s, p95 90ms, NaN rate down to 0.02%. still 4% slower than baseline due to dequant overhead.

maya: sounds good. let's follow up on fusing dequant+kv_write and per-channel accumulation fixes in a separate PR.

lina: opened tracking ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-8429 "fp8 selector: numeric hardening + fused dequant path"

kevin: cool. can we add a small unit test that injects extreme qkv values and asserts no NaNs after kv write? avoids regressions in CI.

dario: will add test and bench microkernel comparisons.

lina: thanks all — closing the loop once we get post-patch perf logs.
